description: We are Lifeline Aerospace, a three-person team passionate about aerospace, space exploration and technology. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are developing a software solution to monitor astronaut sleep schedules and identify unusual trends related to sleep schedules and mental health during long-duration space missions. We bring curiosity, creativity, problem-solving and a willingness to learn. Our team is complete, and we are not recruiting additional members.
summary: We developed an app that can monitor and predict astronaut sleep quality. The app takes into consideration that you are in orbit, the issue that arrises from this is that sunrise occurs 16 times per day, greatly disturbing sleep which is one of the most important aspects for health. This app tracks heart rate in order to keep track of sleep cycles, with the more sleep cycles you go though the higher quality your sleep is.
details:
ORBITAL SLEEP is a web-based crew health monitoring and simulation platform designed to support astronaut wellbeing during space missions. It combines heart-rate data, sleep-cycle modelling, orbital tracking, sunlight exposure, radiation and temperature information in an interactive dashboard.

Users can explore the ISS orbit through 2D and 3D visualisations, monitor environmental conditions and simulate potential effects on crew health. The platform aims to help identify environmental factors that may affect astronaut rest and performance, supporting better-informed decisions for longer missions.

We developed it using claude code for orbital calculations and for data visualisation. Our creative approach combines orbital mechanics, environmental modelling and crew health monitoring in one accessible platform.

During development, we considered data reliability, individual differences, scientific limitations and the distinction between real measurements and simulated outputs.
